frozen.v1: Frozen 2026-08-27 (FUT-956). release-major-tag.yml advances every live major independently and stops each before the first breaking commit — and since no commit has carried a `!` marker or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer since v2 was cut, nothing ever stopped v1. It was dragged the whole way, so `@v1` was not the v1 line at all: it was the current v2 wearing a v1 label, and twenty-nine commits reached `@v1` consumers with nothing to review. Freezing it at that same commit costs those consumers nothing today (the two tags resolve identically) and makes the split visible instead of silent from here on. The tag is deliberately NOT deleted: every `@v1` pin in a consumer keeps resolving exactly what it resolves now, and the migration to `@v2` is a normal PR in the consumer rather than an outage.
